findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached-Hungarian endpoint mean squared distance and native endpoint VJP, so coordinate contrasts are reward-relevant only through that endpoint scalar.

The observed window is the score-time grid 0.0 to 0.49 with learning window [0.0,0.5] and curve support [0.0,0.49]; labels are recorded affinities removed under an equal score prior, so no absolute affinity target is available and contrasts must be interpreted as signed favorable-versus-comparison coordinate differences at observed selection nodes.

Continuous contrast functions for landmark_00 local coordinates are non-monotone across the observed support: landmark_00_local_dx shows 6 sign changes with 9 strong sign conflicts, landmark_00_local_dz shows 10 sign changes with 7 strong sign conflicts, and landmark_00_local_dy shows 6 sign changes with 4 strong sign conflicts, all with polynomial_accepted false and extrapolation_allowed false.

Rate estimates at the window ends are large and opposing for several local coordinates (e.g. landmark_00_local_dx first_rate_z about -17.5 versus last_rate_z about +8.1; landmark_00_local_dy first_rate_z about -72.4 versus last_rate_z about +5.5), while whole-window z values are small and near zero, indicating that endpoint rate magnitudes do not translate into a stable whole-window signed direction.

Landmark soft-mass and local second-moment features also fail to give a stable signed direction: landmark_00_soft_mass has 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict with whole_window_z about 0.64, and landmark_00_local_cyy has 4 sign changes with whole_window_z about -0.58; relative node RMSE values (about 0.29 to 0.78) indicate imperfect fit fidelity for the observed-node linear method.

hypotheses.direction: time-conditioned rather than constant signed contrast on landmark_00 local coordinates
hypotheses.falsifier: A constant-sign contrast with comparable or better fit fidelity and no strong sign conflicts across independent batches would weaken the time-conditioned hypothesis.
hypotheses.observable: signed landmark_00 local coordinate contrast evaluated at observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast rule for landmark_00 local displacement may outperform a constant rule, because the observed-node linear fits show sign changes and opposing endpoint rates within the observed window rather than a single stable sign.

hypotheses.direction: down-weight endpoint-rate-only ranking in favor of whole-window and conflict-aware evidence
hypotheses.falsifier: A feature with large endpoint rates, near-zero sign conflicts and a consistent whole-window sign across independent batches would support rate-magnitude ranking.
hypotheses.observable: whole-window z and strong_sign_conflicts per feature
hypotheses.scope: landmark_00 local coordinate features in the observed window
hypotheses.statement: Prioritizing landmark_00 local coordinate contrasts by endpoint rate magnitude alone is not supported, because large first/last rate z values coexist with near-zero whole-window z and multiple strong sign conflicts.

limitations: Only continuous_trends rows for landmark_00 features were read; branch_adjusted, joint_diagnostics, regional_effects, increment_effects, turnover_accounting, survival_effects and endpoint_effects were not inspected, so multiplicity-adjusted support, independent-batch agreement, coupling and turnover accounting could not be evaluated.
No absolute affinity target is available (recorded affinities removed, equal score prior), so contrasts cannot be converted into an absolute geometric or energetic target.
The supplied evidence does not establish neural-module causation or physical interaction energies; coordinate contrasts are reward-relevant only through the declared endpoint pointcloud scalar.
No current study outcome data are available to this role, so no claim about realized affinity improvement is made.
